story: Gutulia is a forest park. Its old, big-timbered woods drew calls for protection as early as 1916, and it became a national park on 20 December 1968. This is the country of silver-grey dead pines and scattered ancient spruces — trees that have stood for several hundred years and, once fallen, feed a rich life of insects, fungi and lichens. There are few or no traces of forestry. The park rises from about 615 metres around the lakes to 949 metres on Gutulivola, its central fell.

Open pine woods clothe the slopes of Gutulivola; the lower ground carries dense spruce forest full of dead and fallen trees. The soil, mostly poor sandstone, makes the area botanically modest, with the richest variety along streams in the spruce woods. But the old trees shelter many threatened species of fungi and lichens. About 100 species of bird have been recorded, and all four of the large predators — bear, wolf, wolverine and lynx — roam through; bears have bred nearby in recent years.

In contrast to the forest stand the three summer farms of Gutulisetra — Nedpåvollen, Oppåvollen and Lillebovollen — on the park's south-western edge. Farms at Sorken and Lillebo used them each summer from 1750 to 1949, and their old timber buildings are well preserved. The meadows are still mown and kept open, which keeps them full of flowers and the insects that feed on them.

Wild reindeer were wiped out here around 1880, but domestic reindeer still graze the whole park; South Sámi herding here is documented from the 1600s, and the South Sámi community at Gutu herds actively today. When the little Ormtjernkampen National Park was absorbed into Langsua in 2011, Gutulia — enlarged in 2004 to about 23 square kilometres — became Norway's smallest national park.
howItWorks: The right to roam, allemannsretten, applies: you may walk anywhere in the outfield and pick berries and mushrooms. Camping is allowed under the usual rules — two nights in one place without asking, at least 150 metres from a house or cabin — but a tent may not stay more than a week in one place without permission, lean-tos may not be built, and boats and canoes may not be left behind. All vegetation, dead trees included, is protected: never fell or break trees for a fire, and use wood sparingly. From 15 April to 15 September it is forbidden across Norway to light a fire in or near forest and other open country unless the municipality has allowed it or a fire plainly cannot spread; check with Engerdal before you go.

Motor traffic is forbidden on land and water and in the air below 300 metres, and drones may not be flown; under Miljødirektoratet's rule, drones may not take off in a national park or be flown into one without the park board's permission. Cycling and organised riding are allowed only on roads or routes approved in the management plan. Organised activities that could harm the environment need permission.

The only hunting allowed is for moose, under the game law; fishing follows the freshwater fishing law and needs the ordinary licence. Dogs must be on a lead from 1 April to 20 August under the national dog law. Animals and their dens, nests and spawning grounds must not be disturbed.

sightNotes.poi-no-gutulia-gutulisetra: Three summer farms worked from 1750 to 1949, with 16 restored timber buildings and a 1.5 km nature trail; in summer, hosts serve coffee and waffles at Nedpåvollen.
sightNotes.poi-no-gutulia-oppavollen: The uppermost of the three farms, with a small exhibition on two hundred years of summer-farm life.
sightNotes.poi-no-gutulia-gutulivola: The park's central fell, 949 metres, its slopes clothed in open old pine forest.
sightNotes.poi-no-gutulia-valsjoen: A good fishing lake in the mires east of Gutulivola, draining east towards Sweden.
sightNotes.poi-no-gutulia-gutulisjoen: The lake on the park's western edge; the path in follows its shore from the car park.

entrances: The entrance and car park at Gutulisjøen, reached from Femundsenden on Fv 26 by the road towards Elgå and then a signposted forest road of about 3 km; a nature trail of about 3 km leads along the lake to Gutulisetra
planYourVisit.reservations: No booking or fee. The hosts at Gutulisetra are there through the summer.

chronology.text: South Sámi reindeer herding in the area is first documented.
Farms from the valley begin using the Gutulisetra summer pastures.
Wild reindeer are wiped out in the area.
The first proposals are made to protect Gutulia's big old pine forest.
The last summer at the Gutulisetra farms.
Gutulia National Park is created on 20 December, covering about 18 square kilometres.
The park is enlarged on 10 September to about 23 square kilometres.
Gutulia becomes Norway's smallest national park when Ormtjernkampen is absorbed into Langsua.

safety: Beyond the farms there are no marked paths, and the dense spruce forest is easy to get lost in. Carry map and compass.
Fallen trees make for slow, awkward going; watch your footing and allow plenty of time.
Large predators pass through. Make noise in thick forest and never approach a den.
regulations: Never fell or damage trees, living or dead; use wood sparingly for fires.
No drones; no motor traffic on land, water or in the air below 300 metres.
No tent in one place for more than a week, no lean-tos, and no boats or canoes left behind.
No open fires near forest from 15 April to 15 September unless the municipality allows it; dogs on a lead from 1 April to 20 August.

weather: Gutulia is high inland forest, between about 615 and 949 metres above sea level. Summer is the season to come: the hosts are at Gutulisetra through the summer, the meadows are mown and in flower, and the path along Gutulisjøen leads straight to the farms.
directions: Gutulia lies in Engerdal between Drevsjø and Elgå, south of Femundsmarka and on the Swedish border, just south of Fv 221, the road from Elgå towards Idre in Sweden. From Fv 26 at Femundsenden follow the road towards Elgå, then a signposted forest road about 3 km to the entrance at Gutulisjøen; from the car park a trail of about 3 km leads along the lake to Gutulisetra. There is no railway nearby; buses run from Elverum to Engerdal and on to Elgå.
